Lock reason:
MAJOR non-conformity on requirement 4.3.2:
 The site manufactures a private-label Limoncello liqueur (25% vol, 50 cl) for a client based in France. During the review of the product's labeling, several regulatory non-compliances were identified, which were not communicated to the client. This constitutes a breach in the label validation and review process.
 
 The following issues were noted:
 
 1. Misleading claim: The statement “traditional Italian recipe” implies a traditional composition, whereas the product contains a lemon-free flavoring, colorants, and a thickener. This contradicts:
 * Regulation (EU) No. 1169/2011, Article 7 (fair information practices),
 * and Article L121-2 of the French Consumer Code (misleading commercial practices).
 
 2. Ambiguous designation: The phrase “lemon liqueur” used in the marketing presentation suggests the presence of actual lemon ingredients, while it only contains a natural lemon-flavored aroma, with no fruit content. This is non-compliant with:
 * Regulation (EC) No. 1334/2008, Article 16,
 * and the DGCCRF practical guide – November 2017 (highlighted claims and ingredient representation).
 
 3. Graphic representation: The use of lemon illustrations on the front and back of the label is not accompanied by an immediate mention such as “lemon-flavored” or equivalent, which may mislead the consumer. This also breaches Regulation (EC) No. 1334/2008 and DGCCRF recommendations.
 
 The private-label client validated the label in 2022 based on the recipe provided by the site and conducted an audit in 2024 without identifying these irregularities. The site did not inform the client of the regulatory non-compliances identified since, which constitutes a failure in the duty to inform and manage regulatory changes.
 
 This finding highlights a failure in the label control procedure, in regulatory monitoring, as well as in communication with the client regarding the legal requirements applicable to private-label products.
 
 It should be noted that this is an isolated case among more than 30,000 products manufactured at the site. The current label verification procedure now effectively detects this type of error for new labels, unlike the present case, which dates back to 2016. A verification conducted on a new label for a similar product has demonstrated the effectiveness of the current procedure.

1.2.1 KO
 In accordance with the standard, management must ensure that employees are aware of their responsibilities with regard to food safety and product quality and that mechanisms are in place to monitor the effectiveness of their actions. These mechanisms are identified and documented. This is not implemented to a sufficient extent; for example, an internal audit conducted by an external auditor on 20-21 August 2024 identified a total of 65 deviations (31x of which were D deviations and 8x of which were major/KO) without sufficient measures being taken by the company management to effectively remedy the numerous significant deviations. Another example would be, for example, that a simple production employee, who can only communicate in German to a very limited extent, was tasked with the daily documentation of the raw material batches used in pita production; during the IP check, it was observed that the daily documentation of the raw material batches used has been missing since 30 May 2025, which the company has not noticed to date. There is no control or assurance that the employee is carrying out this important documentation correctly in accordance with the specifications. Furthermore, the large number of deviations and non-conformities identified during the IFS IP check is an indication that the responsibility of the company management is not being taken into account to a sufficiently effective extent.
 2.3.9.4 Major
 Monitoring CP Protective fumigation of finished goods Pita rolls in tubular bags not under sufficient control: The monitoring of the protective fumigation of pita rolls in tubular bags is defined as CP; corresponding checks must be carried out at the beginning, then every 30 minutes and at the end, whereby the residual oxygen in the packaging must not exceed 1.1%. The company cannot conclusively justify the monitoring criterion. There is also no validation available for the monitoring process. During the plant tour, all residual oxygen measurements recorded on the current production day were, without exception, below the monitoring criterion of max. 1.1% residual oxygen. The auditor then initiated 5 random samples of the current production; all random samples of the finished goods were significantly above the 1.1% residual oxygen (= between 1.89 and 2.5% residual oxygen). In the further course, random samples were taken from the production of the previous days as well as from the stored retained samples; the random samples of the previous day's production consistently showed values between 2.3-2.4%. In the case of the retained samples, only 2 values were below the monitoring criterion of 1.1%; in others, peak values of 6.48% (= pita production with BBD 04.07.2025) up to 8.3% residual oxygen were observed (= pita production with BBD 17.07.2025). The measuring device used for monitoring (=Oxibaby) should be calibrated at least once a week according to internal specifications, but was last verifiably calibrated on 06.05.2025. According to the specification (work instruction CP 3 / version 8 as of 05.11.2024), further measurements should be carried out if the measured values deviate from 1.1% residual oxygen; if the limit value is confirmed to have been exceeded, all packages must be re-measured from the last good test; random samples with limit value exceedances must then be unpacked and repacked. The fact is that almost all of the residual oxygen checks initiated by the auditor showed, in some cases, greatly increased, deviating test results. According to the shift supervisor, it is known that the residual oxygen value in the packaging increases again after the residual oxygen test immediately after packaging; this could be due to interaction with the packaged product or also to leaks or insufficient tightness of the packaging, although documented tightness tests of the Pita-Roll tubular bag pre-packaging are not planned. Residual oxygen monitoring is insufficiently defined (what, when and where) and the company's monitoring results contradict the spot checks initiated by the auditor, which cannot be conclusively justified by the company.

The product-specific requirements in this regard can be found in the document Overview of core temperatures 4_AA_#0498 (V1/10.07.2024).
 
 The company produces sous-vide products in two different production areas, in the so-called ‘large scale’ area where large quantities/volumes of sous-vide products are produced, which are primarily marketed as pre-packaged products in the food retail trade. For the sous-vide products produced here in industrial cooking cabinets, compliance with the relevant CCP criteria can be demonstrated in a traceable manner via electronic temperature/time records (=recording of heating temperature, holding time and cooling temperature with cooling times).
 To date, this has not been the case for small-batch sous vide production in the production kitchen, which is intended for bulk consumers/catering customers. Here, for each sous vide production batch in a conventional manual cooking cabinet (without automatic temperature/time recording), only the time at which the product reached the specified heating temperature is recorded; the re-cooling time required for the product to cool to a core temperature of less than 10°C after the heating process is also documented.  Major on 4.3.2: 
 Deviation on final product labelling:
 - Observed a dried cured salami sausage with written statement/claim Wagyu beef of which only the 20% Wagyu Beef meat part was of Wagyu. The animal protein (muscle) parts of this product were of conventional beef species 94%.
 From the recipe it was observed that the 20% Wagyu Beef meat which related to 100% Wagyu Beef fat should have been declared as beef fat and not as beef meat.
 - A couple of raw prepared sausages follow the process flow that after preparation and packing these were internally frozen. Based on customer order these products were thawed prior to dispatch and delivered (unfrozen, 'fresh') to their clients. However, no references on labelling information made with regards to the "defrosted"-state of this meat preparation.
 From the validation report on thawing and microbiological shelf life tests based on Salmonella and Listeria monocytogenes and supported by sensory analyses after thawing. Despite no microbiological decay bacteria have been included in these tests on expiry (such as Pseudomonas, Enterobacteriaceae, Lactic acid) result show no increase in decay after thawing. 
 In consolidated issue of this EU Regulation (dated 01.04.2025) no references to art.28 exists anymore referring to 'The freezing and later defrosting of certain foods, especially meat and fishery products, limits their possible further use and may also have an effect on their safety, taste and physical quality'-By means no exclusion on topic 2c could be applicable.
 The companies own interpretation on this subject resulted that the label interpretation has been incorporated based on the exclusion at reference on 'defrosting' in EU 1169/2011 Annex VI part A.2c 'foods for which the defrosting has no negative impact on the safety or quality of the food'. 
 - There are a couple of products artisanal smoked on beach wood and create an organoleptic taste experience of this smoke. No use of artificial smoke aromas/flavouring in place.
 Observed that in the ingredient label no references were made to the smoke flavouring even though this taste is naturally created by smoking the product on beech wood flakes. Some of these articles have a final product sleeve where reference is made to natural smoke flavour achieved by beech wood flakes. 
 Though for a couple of new introduced hotdogs labels derive from ERP-system Reflex and no reference on the origin of the smoke flavour was incorporated. 
 
 Even though this labelling based on law and regulation is incorrect. There was no direct food safety or health impact on final consumer. Immediate actions were taken , such as stock, product delivery and labels are blocked, request for verification by expert team from Pander Consultancy on these discrepancies.

During the audit and verification of the inventory records for a raw material, it was found that traceability was neither guaranteed nor documented for the batch of alpha amylase enzymes, product reference 5005, batch number 144500, with a best-before date of October 30, 2025. This batch was received in a quantity of 25 kg, but computer records show consumption of 3.3 kg of the product used for the manufacture of organic soil improver mixes. The inventory on the day of the audit showed a stock level of 0. An inventory count indicated that the batch had been removed at the end of July (presumably because the product was not located during the inventory).
 However, this batch was used in the manufacture of a mix on November 19, 2025 (the first day of the audit), with a quantity of 800 g used. This product is used at a concentration of 0.3% in the only recipe for which it is used. The operator stated that they finished the bag of alpha amylase on November 19, 2025, and discarded the empty carton. The carton was found in the cardboard recycling bin.
 The mass balance for the product used showed a 21.7 kg difference, indicating an inconsistency in the material accounting.
 After investigation, the operator admitted to discarding the remaining 21.7 kg because the expiration date had passed and to concealing this information.
 The system did not block the production of the mixture, even though the theoretical computerized stock for this raw material was zero following the July inventory. The production run of November 19, 2025, was recorded in the computer system without being blocked, despite the expiration date of the alpha amylase raw material having passed.

KO 5.1.1: A risk assessment on the basis of which activities critical to food safety and product quality are audited more frequently is not available.  KO 5.11.3: Not all corrective measures were implemented in such a way as to prevent the recurrence of devi-ations and non-conformities. As in the previous year, products were filled or placed on the market without the labelled best-before date being validated.
 
 Major 4.3.4: When 1 kg sales units are picked, they are labelled during picking. This label contains the batch identi-fication and the calculation of the best-before date based on the picking date, not the production date. However, products that were not filled on the picking date and whose best-before date was calculated based on the production date as specified are also processed. In order to avoid an unvalidated best-before date extension, the best-before date of the 1 kg sales units was shortened by three days com-pared to the other sales units. However, there is no clear instruction that products older than three days may no longer be picked. During the audit, products were repeatedly seen that exceeded this three-day period, e.g. couscous salad batch 251114 and Strasbourg sausage salad batch 251114. Both products were produced on 14 November 2025 and sold on 19 November 2025, i.e. five days later. This resulted in an unvalidated extension of the best-before date by two days, with a total best-before date of 16 days. This means that delicatessen salads are being placed on the market whose shelf life has not been determined on the basis of validation.
 
 Major 4.4.1: The procedure for purchasing packaging materials is not documented, implemented and maintained in such a way that legal requirements are met. There is no established process to ensure that new packaging materials are tested for conformity before being placed on the market. During the IFS Food audit carried out from November 25 to 27, 2025, a major non-conformity was detected regarding requirement 4.5.2
 Chemical risks associated with packaging are governed by group procedures, in particular by a packaging charter dated November 2024 (prohibiting the use of phthalates, bisphenol, nano and mineral oils, and requiring the use of low-migration inks).
 This has been explored for Poule et Toque brand direct-contact labels used on frozen whole chickens under the packaging film.
 The documents provided were:
 - a proof approved on April 24, 2023
 - a declaration of conformity dated July 2, 2024 from supplier G
 - and a declaration of conformity dated February 19, 2025 from the same supplier, submitted during the closing meeting.
  
 Major non-compliance:
 - The first declaration of compliance stipulates that the label adhesive must be used on a barrier, or in contact with a dry, non-greasy product, or requires appropriate migration tests. The migration tests were carried out with 10% and 20% ethanol and Tenax, solvents that correspond to dry foodstuffs (which is not suitable for chicken skin).
 - Following this observation made on the first day of the audit, several other labels in direct contact were set aside on the second day because their guarantees were not sufficient according to management (e.g., labels for the ID Halal, Cocotte, and SEBIL brands).
 - For the Poulets Fermiers Argoat label (manufactured by another label supplier, A.), the declaration of conformity submitted on the second day of the audit did not correspond to the label reference.
 - The declaration of conformity dated February 19, 2025, submitted at the closing meeting, also does not provide all the necessary guarantees: for the paper, it does not mention compliance with regulatory texts, purity criteria, or inertia criteria. It does not mention the other components of the label, which nevertheless appear on the proof ( primary inks and 2 Pantone colors in particular) and for which the usual guarantees, in particular those of EUPIA, are not provided.
  
 This shows that the guarantees allowing verification of the absence of any negative effects from labels in direct contact with meat have not been sufficiently verified.
 This does not concern the two private labels (which are customers for products packaged in trays under atmosphere and labeled on the sealing film), but at the time of the audit, whole chickens were labeled in direct contact with labels for which the guarantees are incomplete

NC Major item 5.5.1 :
 During the flow freeze line, on which the pork sauté (own branded Jean Floch), batch 25322, was being packaged in 5kg bags, it was found that for the series of 10 weighings in progress, the % of TU1 was 10%. Operators are required to perform 3 series of 10 weighings per hour. The weighing results are recorded in the weighing software, which generates a “Stat1” for each series of 10 weighings and a ‘Stat2’ corresponding to the overall evaluation of the weighed batch. The “Stats” show the average and the associated %TU1 and %TU2 for each one. The E/79/02-16 freezing tracking sheet for the batch in progress, on which (among other things) the weight control results are indicated, had been completed with a cross in the section provided for “Validation of the Stat1 series.” When questioned, the operator being audited stated that she had placed a cross in the box dedicated to this check to certify that the weighings had been carried out, but that she did not interpret the results. At the auditor's request, the weight control results for the entire batch 25322 of the sauté mentioned above were printed and are as follows: average 5018.7g - % TU1 2.05% and %TU2: 1.37%. However, these results do not certify the conformity of the weight of the packaged batch and do not meet the requirements of Decree 78-166, which states that: 
 - The actual content of the pre-packaged items in the batch must not be less than the nominal content on average;
 - The proportion of prepackages with an error less than the maximum permissible error indicated in the table below must be sufficiently low to enable batches of prepackages to satisfy the statistical tests of official control. As the acceptance rate for these tests is 2.5%, the DGCCRF's “Guide to good practice concerning internal metrological control procedures to be carried out by pre-packagers” of July 2014 sets a maximum defect rate of 2%. This maximum TU1 rate was also clearly specified in the instruction for carrying out weight checks on the Flowfreeze IC/79/04-05 line of April 2024.
 The same instruction states that if the first series of weighings indicates non-compliant results (based on the average or %TU1 criterion), a second series of 10 weighings must be carried out. If this second series is also non-compliant, the products must be separated from the last compliant batch and weighed individually.
 
 However, for the batch in question:
 - The operator clearly stated that she did not interpret the results in any specific way, and the percentage of non-compliant TU1 was noted by the auditor.
 - Any corrections that may have been made following the discovery of the non-compliant series were not documented, and the site cannot certify that the batch has been brought back into compliance.
 As things stand, the site cannot certify the compliance of batch 25322 or the effectiveness of the currently defined procedure.
 In general, it was confirmed that the results associated with the weighing of packaged batches, and in particular the “stat 2” results for the batches, were archived in a directory but were not analyzed by a person named for the site. In the absence of analysis, the site cannot prove that there have been no other findings of this type.
 It should be noted, however, that following this finding, five other results associated with sauté packaging days were verified by sampling, and no other non-compliant results were identified during this consultation.

Supplier: SALAISONS CELTIQUES SAS - Site de St Meen le Grand .
Lock reason:
Major non-compliance with requirement § 4.3.2
 -During the audit, the traceability test focused on the following product: "Surprise de porc cuite goût fumé marinée au poivre et baies rose", a private label product.
 During the audit, three points of non-compliance with the regulations (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011) were identified:
  --The list of ingredients on the label of the product "Surprise de porc cuite goût fumé marinée au poivre et baies rose" mentions the following quantities of ingredients: 2.7% black pepper and 2.7% pink peppercorns. These ingredients are present in the finished product only as part of the ingredient ‘pepper and pink peppercorn seasoning’ (this ingredient is part of the marinade used in the product). When consulting the technical data sheet of the supplier of this seasoning (technical data sheet dated 16/12/2024 from supplier F... C...), it was seen that the supplier declares, in addition to other ingredients, the presence of 21% pepper in the seasoning and 5% pink peppercorns. The seasoning therefore contains more pepper than pink peppercorns. As a result, there is an inconsistency between the quantities of pink peppercorns declared in the technical data sheet and those declared in the list of ingredients: since the quantities of pepper and peppercorns are different in the raw material, it is not possible for these ingredients to be present in equal quantities in the finished product (as a reminder, the recipe for the product ‘smoked pork surprise marinated in pepper and pink peppercorns’ does not include the addition of pink peppercorns in addition to the seasoning). 
 After consulting the file used by the site to calculate QUIDs, which was used for the product in question in this case, it was found that the seasoning data used by the site to define QUIDs was incorrect because it did not match the supplier's technical data sheet. This file indicates a percentage of 23% pepper and 19% pink peppercorns.
 This defect means that the requirements of Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Article 7, cannot be met: ‘1. Food information shall not be misleading, in particular: (a) as to the characteristics of the food, and in particular as to its nature, (...), composition, quantity (...)’; "2. Food information shall be specific, clear (...)‘ and Article 8 ’2. The food business operator responsible for food information shall ensure that food information is present and accurate (...)".
  --Furthermore, after consulting with the R&D manager and reviewing the file used by the site to calculate QUIDs for the product in question, it was found that the percentages of ingredients declared in the compound ingredient ‘marinade’ " (i.e. 4% smoke flavouring, 2.7% pepper and 2.7% pink peppercorns) are declared on the marinade (the finished product contains 14.7% marinade) and not on the finished product. In fact, using the values for pepper and pink peppercorns declared by the seasoning supplier (in the technical data sheet dated 16/12/2024 from supplier F... C...), the finished product contains 0.45% pepper and 0.11% pink peppercorns.
 Declaring the quantities of ingredients in the marinade does not meet the requirements of Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, as the Regulation requires that ingredients be declared on the finished product in order to provide clear information to consumers. This is specified in Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex VIII, point 3: the quantity of an ingredient must be expressed as a percentage and corresponds to the quantity of one or more ingredients at the time of use. Here, processing corresponds to the moment when the marinade is added to the meat, i.e. the quantity of pepper on the one hand and pink peppercorns on the other hand in the meat + marinade mixture. Furthermore, indicating the quantities of ingredients in the marinade leads to percentages that are clearly higher than the actual quantities. This shortcoming means that the requirements of Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Article 7, cannot be met: “1. Food information shall not be misleading, in particular: (a) as to the characteristics of the food, and in particular as to its nature, (...), composition, quantity (...)”, '2. Food information shall be accurate, clear (...)‘ and Article 8 ’2. The food business operator responsible for food information shall ensure the presence and accuracy of food information (...)".
  --For the product tested for traceability, the legal name used is "Surprise de porc cuite goût fumé marinée au poivre et baies rose". Furthermore, in the list of ingredients, the meat component is declared under the name “surprise de porc”.
 Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Article 17(1), requires that sales names be legal, customary or descriptive. In the case of the product tested for traceability, the name must be descriptive (definition of a descriptive name given in Article 2 of Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011: a name that describes the food and, where necessary, its use, and is sufficiently clear for consumers to determine its true nature and distinguish it from other products with which it could be confused) . The name must therefore be understandable to consumers and must enable them to know the true nature of the product. 
 According to Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Article 18(2), it is stated that ‘ingredients shall be designated by their specific name’ in the list of ingredients.
 After requesting justification for the name ‘surprise de porc’, the site provided a document from the IFIP (Institut du Porc) dated 2014, which uses this name to describe a muscle located on top of the pork shoulder blade. This document specifies that ‘surprise de porc’ is a ‘dénomination bouchère’. This term is therefore a professional term and not a common term.
 The use of a professional term in the legal sales name on the one hand and in the list of ingredients on the other does not provide clear information to consumers or meet the requirements for the list of ingredients, as a professional term is not a ‘specific’ term (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Article 7: 2. Information on foodstuffs shall be accurate, clear and easily understandable by consumers).
 It should be noted that the term ‘surprise de porc’ does not appear in the decree of 18/03/1993 and its current amendments, which lists the usual names for meat products in Annex I.

Supplier: Société Fermière Rochefort Ardennes - Etablissements Mathot SPRL
Lock reason:
4.3.2-Major 
 Regarding the development of new products such as flavoured butter, the company does not have a procedure to ensure that the labelling is in accordance with the legislation in force in the country/countries of destination.
 Indeed, for the "Yuzu Butter" brand Rochefort, (3 productions of "Yuzu Butter" concerned: manufacture of 30/10/25 (lot 303), 31/10/25 (lot 304), 29/11/25 (lot 333) for a total quantity of 1116 kg, mainly, but not only, sold to the client DEXXX), it was found several anomalies or inaccuracies of labelling:
 1. The labelling communicates a single commercial and legal name: 'Yuzu Butter'. However, in the list of ingredients, the following QUID (or Quantitative indication of ingredients) are not mentioned: % butter, % Yuzu, % salt.
 On the other hand, the list of ingredients indicates for QUID du Yuzu (which is the dextrin mixture, yuzu juice) a percentage of 4.8%. However, the recipe indicates a theoretical percentage of 4.76% at implementation and the actual quantity implemented calculated on the average of the 3 batches manufactured is 4.48%. The labeled Quid is therefore not representative of the percentage of yuzu juice actually implemented and guaranteed. Therefore, the labelling does not appear in accordance with Article 22, point 1, of Regulation R1169/2011 EC.
 Finally, the name is not explicit on the fact that the butter is salted butter although salt is indeed mentioned in the list of ingredients.
 2. The labelled list of ingredients mention: yuzu (yuzu juice, dextrin)4.8%. The name of the ingredient as mentioned appears ambiguous since the ingredient added for flavoring purposes is not yuzu «fruit», but a preparation based on yuzu composed of dextrin as a majority component and yuzu juice. Therefore, the latter does not appear in accordance with Annex VII, PART E—DESIGNATION OF COMPOUND INGREDIENTS of Regulation R1169/2011 EC.
 On the other hand, the compound ingredient is listed as: yuzu juice, dextrin. Therefore, the descending order of components of as required by Article 18(1) of Regulation R1169/2011 EC is not respected.
 3.The only name present on the finished product is 'Yuzu butter'. The labelling does not mention another legal name. Now the recipe contains dextrin which, although added for the purpose of
 supporting yuzu juice and not as a loading agent, is present in a non-negligible percentage (see supplier’s KEXXX technical sheet version dated 27/05/25 - ingredients: dextrin, yuzu juice). Therefore, the legitimacy of using the designation 'Yuzu butter' does not appear to be clearly established within the meaning of Article 3 (1) of European Regulation No 445/2007 EC defining the applicable rules allowing the use of the designation 'butter' for composite products. Indeed, although the milk fat of the finished product is > 75% (76.92%), all the components added to the butter are not mentioned in the name. Only 'Yuzu' appears there. On the other hand, the non-negligible share of dextrin does not guarantee its absence of a 'texturing effect' in the finished product.
 In view of these findings, the labelling validation system does not guarantee that the labelling complies with the legislation in force in the destination country/countries and in particular with the requirements of Regulation R1169/2011 EC. Therefore, a Major non-compliance is assigned to the site on requirement 4.3.2

Following Integrity on site check in date 13/01/2026 and after preliminary technical review and decision, the certificate is suspended for the following reasons:
 IFS Food Standard § 5.11.3 KO
 In 2025, the company received 11 complaints regarding incorrect labeling (name, expiration dates). Furthermore, customer C. noted several consumer complaints regarding browning of pork coppa with a dedicated brand.
 The company had been packaging the product in MAP, using vacuum-packed raw materials until the raw materials' expiration date, extending the product's shelf life by an additional 10 days once packaged in MAP. A company validation study found that pork coppa in MAP browns on the 7th and 8th day, respectively, if packaged from raw materials with a residual shelf life of 7 and 8 days. For this reason, as a corrective action, the company has decided not to use vacuum-packed raw materials beyond their 10-day shelf life.
 On the day of the IOC, a traceability test was carried out on the product boneless sliced pork coppa, with a brand dedicated for retailer C. batch 15 337 178, shipped with a transport document dated 04.12.2025, packaged in ATM with an expiry date of 13.12.2025. From the verification of the label kept on the day of packaging, it emerged that the name shown on the label was incorrect (it was “Fettina di lombo di suino” and not “Coppa di suino”). Furthermore, two batches of raw material were used for this product, one of which expired on 11.12.2025. From the traceability of the batch of raw material with an expiry date of 11.12.2025, it emerged that another batch of pork coppa (L 15336179) with an expiry date of 12.12.2025 was also produced with this raw material. In both batches, the product's shelf life exceeds the raw material's shelf life, and the requirement to use the raw material only within its 10-day residual shelf life was not met for both batches.
 Furthermore, the company did not conduct a shelf-life study to support the decision to pack the product, starting with the raw material with a 10-day residual shelf life, in order to ensure product compliance until the expiration date.
 In the validation study conducted (on raw material with a 7- and 8-day residual shelf life), only one batch of raw material was tested, and the variability and evolution of the modified atmosphere were not evaluated, to extend the observations observed for a single batch to all batches.

KO_2.3.9.1:
 The company has defined CCP2 as the control of the rinse water pressure for empty glass bottles prior to filling, with a monitoring frequency at the start of production, middle, and at the end of the process. This control is performed through inspection of the pressure gauge of the empty bottle rinsing equipment and applies to both empty still wine bottles and empty sparkling wine bottles.
 During the on site plant inspection carried out on 22-01-2026, it was observed that the bottle rinsing equipment was not in operation due to a breakdown, therefore the empty bottle rinsing was not being carried out and, consequently, the corresponding CCP2 control was not carried out. [product being filled: sparkling wine – cava, tirage CB13GSCBECO].
 The company has neither implemented nor documented any corrective action related to this incident.
 Several process records were reviewed in order to determine when CPP2 control has not been performed. The following evidence was obtained from the review of the available records:
 - The “Breakdowns and Repairs Register” (R10 P4), in which equipment failures must be recorded, was reviewed. It was determined that the breakdown of the empty bottle rinsing equipment is not recorded, therefore it is not possible to determine the exact start date of the breakdown through this register.
 - The R03 P09 “Line Control” record, under the Maintenance Activities Register section, which includes daily checks before and after use of the equipment in the tirage area, including the bottle rinsing machine, was reviewed. For 22-01-2026, the bottle rinsing machine status is recorded as “OK before use”. For 21-01-2026, the bottle rinsing machine is recorded as “OK before use” and “OK after use”. Therefore, it is not possible to determine the exact start date of the breakdown through this register.
 - The CCP2 monitoring record R04 P03 “Internal Bottle Cleaning Check” was also reviewed. This review confirmed that no CCP2 monitoring records are available for either 21-01-2026 or 22-01-2026. Complete and compliant records, including rinsing pressure values greater > 2 bar and monitoring frequency, are available for 20, 19, 16 and 15-01-2026.
 Based on the analysis of the records reviewed, it is concluded that the empty bottle rinsing equipment has been out of order since 21-01-2026, and that CCP2 monitoring has not been performed since that date, meaning that this Critical Control Point has been out of control since then. The products manufactured on this line since 21-01-2026 correspond to sparkling wine: cava, tirage CB13GSCBECO.
 During the two audit days, the company continued filling the product (sparkling wine – cava, tirage CB13GSCBECO), stating that subsequently, after the bottle fermentation stage, during the disgorging and expedition liqueur dosage stage, all sparkling wine bottles are inspected by the CCP3 optical inspector. This equipment allows the rejection of bottles containing foreign bodies larger than 4 mm, according to the annual verification report issued by the equipment manufacturer (AICxx, report ref 2482-2025 04-08-2025).
 However, this additional control measure is not applicable to still wine bottles, as these do not pass through the disgorging stage and are therefore not subject to CCP3 control.
 Finally, it is considered that the existence of an additional CCP3 control for sparkling wines at the disgorging stage does not compensate for the absence of CCP2 control since 21-01-2026, as, according to the company HACCP document R02 P3, revision 17, CCP2 applies to all manufactured products, including both still wines and sparkling wines.

Major nonconformity to requirement 4.12.9:
 Glass fragments were found on the closing machine of the peanut butter filling line in close proximity to open jars prior to sealing. The glass breakage occurred at approximately 10:30. Following the incident, partial cleaning was carried out by production personnel.
 After this partial cleaning, production was resumed. At the time of the auditor’s observation at 11:15, the line was in operation and open jars were present on the line. No glass fragments were observed in the front part of the line or on the floor, and some glass fragments had been collected and disposed of. However, glass fragments were still found in the rear part of the closing machine, which is less accessible and not routinely frequented by personnel. This demonstrates that cleaning was not performed thoroughly and across the entire affected area.
 The glass breakage was not recorded in the relevant glass incident log and the defined procedure was not fully applied. Products and jars within the defined 2-metre radius from the breakage point were not removed, and it was not demonstrated that a complete, systematic and verified cleaning of all relevant parts of the equipment and surrounding area was performed prior to resumption of production.
 Products manufactured during the time of the incident were not immediately placed on hold. The decision to place the affected products on hold was taken by production management only following a question raised by the auditor during a management discussion on the following day.
 The company has a documented procedure for handling glass breakage incidents, including requirements for recording the incident, removing product within a defined radius and performing thorough cleaning. According to available records, personnel are regularly trained in this procedure and similar incidents were appropriately managed in the past. In this case, however, the procedure was not implemented in full and with the required effectiveness.

Lock reason:
During the audit performed on 20th January 2026 to 22th January 2026, it was detected a Major non-conformity under the requirement 4.19.3.
 
 Major non-conformity 4.19.3.
 
 The company has not been able to demonstrate that the system implemented to ensure that allergen information is transmitted correctly and in accordance with legal requirements is effectively in place.
 
 - The allergen information in the allergen list D.68.00, updated 23/10/2025, is inadequate in some cases. The product "Torreznos" (crispy pork rinds) is included, which shows cross-contamination with sulfites and soy, although this declaration is not made for pressed pork rinds, as they are stored in a separate room. The list does not distinguish between pressed and loose pork rinds, so the information is inadequate.
 
 - The allergen information in the finished product specifications is inconsistent in some cases, although the intended use includes "not suitable for those with sulfite and soy allergies." The label content is not clearly stated. In the ingredient list for fresh sausage, E221 and E224 are not highlighted or identified as "Sulfites," and the phrase "May contain" is included when sulfites are present as ingredients.
 
 - The information included on the label of extra spicy sausage is inconsistent and does not reflect the actual allergenic nature of the product. The label for extra spicy sausage states "May contain soy and sulfites" when sulfites (E221 and E224) are present in quantities exceeding 10 ppm, according to calculations performed during the audit.
 
 - The company has been unable to demonstrate or validate this statement. Calculations performed during the audit show that at least 175 ppm of sulfites are present, a fact unknown to the company. - In some cases, it could not be demonstrated that the label content was correct from an allergen information standpoint, since in at least 17 production runs between April and December, the control records did not include a copy of the label or evidence that its content had been reviewed.
 
 Based on the findings described, it is evident that the company does not have an adequate system in place to guarantee the reliability of the information transmitted to the food chain regarding the allergen content of the manufactured products, as required by law (Regulation 1169/2011 and Regulation 178/2002). The company has not been able to demonstrate sufficient knowledge of these legal requirements for consumer information regarding allergenic ingredients, therefore a Major Non-Conformity (NC) has been issued.

2.3.9.1-KO (D)
 Monitoring of CCP No. 5 is based on checking the core temperature of gyozas at the exit of the cooking tunnel. Monitoring is carried out every 15 minutes. During this audit, the operator responsible for this CCP was interviewed and explained that if the core temperature is non-compliant, the anomaly is immediately reported to the line supervisor to stop production, and that all products exiting the oven are discarded as soon as the anomaly is detected. However, the operator stated that non-compliant temperatures observed are not recorded, and that production only resumes once compliant core temperatures are reached again.
 A case from the previous day (production dated 11 February 2026) was mentioned. The line supervisor confirmed a boiler issue that generated non-compliant temperatures, leading to line stoppage and destruction of the products in the tunnel. Both the person in charge of temperature monitoring and the line supervisor confirmed that non-compliant temperatures are not recorded because the products are destroyed. In the related production file, temperature measurements were recorded every 15 minutes and all recorded temperatures were compliant. However, there was indeed a production stoppage of at least 20 minutes at the cooking tunnel.
 The production file therefore does not reflect the actual situation: non-compliant temperatures were not documented, stoppage times were not specified, and although products were discarded as soon as the anomaly was detected, the planned corrective actions namely blocking products manufactured since the last compliant check were not implemented.
 
 
 4.1.3-KO(D)
 A traceability test was conducted on the product: Cooked vegetable rice private label in 500 g bags; item code: RSS500PC1142; Recipe R1142; client specifications and product specifications validated on 27/06/2025.
 
 Several anomalies were identified during this audit, preventing assurance that the recipe for Cooked Vegetable Rice in 500 g bags (item code: RSS500PC1142; Recipe R1142) is being followed.
 1) In the production record of September 8, 2025, the quantity of dry rice used does not match the manufacturing order (1,840 kg planned vs. 2,490 kg used), while the quantities of the other ingredients (vegetable marking mix, oil, and sauce) were not modified. As the process is continuous, the company explains that rice flow rates are fixed and that additional rice was added to consume the full vegetable marking mix. However, the recording completed in the mixing area, showing the flow rates of the vegetable marking mix and rice, is not available. Normally, it includes the hourly checks of mix and rice flow rates. Without this information, it is not possible to verify that the proportions were respected.
 2) The line operator interviewed during the visit on February 11, 2026 (same product in production) indicated that rice flow rate control (kg/h) is no longer performed, as the flow is fixed and non-adjustable. Therefore, it is not possible to verify the quantity of rice used in relation to the quantity of vegetable marking mix, while the quantities of dry rice used can vary depending on the production day.
 3) Instructions regarding the flow rates for the automatic dosing of oil, rice, and sauce were slightly modified between the production on September 8, 2025, and the current instructions. The reasons for these modifications are not justified, and the impact on the original recipe has not been assessed.
 4) During product development, a final recipe adjustment was made at the client’s request to reduce the cabbage content in the finished product. This resulted in a final version of the recipe with modifications for three ingredients in the vegetable marking mix: sunflower oil (1% → 1.3%), tapioca flour (2% → 1.5%), and cabbage (19% → 18.2%). The final version of the recipe indicated in the client’s specifications was not implemented in production. Production still follows the previous version.
 5) Vegetables are thawed by immersion in hot water and weighed after draining. The weight of the vegetables after thawing should be checked and quantities adjusted in the cooker if necessary, as weight instructions relate to thawed vegetables. During the visit on February 11, the operator’s weighings showed discrepancies between the planned quantities and the actual quantities weighed. The operator weighs and records all bins but never adjusts the quantities, despite discrepancies exceeding the internal tolerance of 1 kg. Internal instructions are not followed. Note that the quantity of frozen vegetables used is nevertheless in accordance with the labeled values.
